notes: Adds a GM soundboard for one-shot SFX (motion sensor bips, metal clanging, that kind of thing), built to a fairly detailed spec Dan handed off. A new 'Soundboard' section in GM Tools, below Ambient Music, shows a 3x3 grid of nine slots. Each slot has an editable label (defaults to 'Slot N'), an audio upload (reuses the existing /api/upload endpoint), a Play button, and a Clear button. Hitting Play broadcasts a one-off 'soundboard:play' socket event to everyone in the room (including the GM's own client) carrying that slot's audio URL - every client immediately constructs an Audio() and plays it once, on top of whatever ambient music is already playing, no ducking. Only the GM sees the soundboard panel at all; a non-GM player gets zero UI/toast/visual cue, just the sound itself. A single master volume slider at the top of the Soundboard section controls playback loudness on the GM's own browser only (localStorage, never synced to the server or other players) - players are expected to use their own system/browser volume. Slot config (label + uploaded file) persists with the room like everything else (survives a server restart), backfilled to 9 blank slots for any room saved before this shipped. To test: open GM Tools as the GM, confirm the Soundboard section with 9 slots appears below Ambient Music; upload an audio file into a slot and give it a custom label, confirm Play is disabled until a file is loaded; hit Play and confirm you hear it, and confirm a second player in the same room (on any tab, not just looking at anything soundboard-related) also hears it with no visual indication on their screen at all; reload the page and Resume the game, confirm the label and uploaded file are still there; hit Clear and confirm it resets both the label and audio back to blank; confirm a non-GM player never sees any soundboard UI anywhere.
